title: Quad-layout cross field stage: 0.40 s to under 100 ms
description: Make the `cross field` stage of QuadLayoutEngine fast. It takes 0.395 s today. The log breaks it down as assemble 0.085, solve aligned 0.150, populate 0.042, build load vector 0.020, hopf 0.019. Baseline, measured 2026-10-15 with `uv run ixdar-cli run-scene --scene quad-layout --property quadLayoutScene.alpha=15` on the default model (headless, 9.1 s to ready): cross field 0.395 s, seamless 0.800 s, motorcycle graph 0.145 s, quantization 1.526 s, carve 0.674 s, contract 1.475 s, global grid map 1.897 s. These run synchronously before the scene's first frame, so together they are almost all of the quad-layout scene's time to first paint. The user's goal is first paint under 0.1 s; a sibling ticket moves the pipeline off the first frame, and each stage ticket makes one stage as fast as it can go. Target: this stage under 100 ms on the default model, or as close as the algorithm allows, with the reason it can go no lower. The stage's output must not change: same singularity count, arc/node/patch counts, quad count and a screenshot that image-diffs clean against the master baseline. Use the stage's own `[quad-layout] <stage>` log line and an async-profiler capture (`run-scene --profile`, read with `ixdar-cli profile-report`). Stay inside this stage's package; touch shared code (solver/, HalfEdgeMesh, QuadLayoutEngine) only where the stage needs it, and list every shared-file change in the report, because six sibling tickets run in parallel. Related: CRAW-2 (scan-scale pipeline), CRAW-4 (cached layouts).
definition-of-done:
1. The stage's `[quad-layout] cross field` time on the default quad-layout model is recorded before and after (median of 3 runs) in changes-made, with the after time under 100 ms or a stated reason it cannot be. 2. Singularity count, arc/node/patch counts and quad count match master exactly. 3. A screenshot of the final layout under tmp/ image-diffs clean against a master screenshot taken the same way. 4. No debugging scaffolding is left behind; `ixd wt done` passes.

5. Whole-suite check: `python3 /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/tmp/quad-suite/run_suite.py --checkout <this worktree> --out /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/tmp/quad-suite/<ticket> --compare /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/tmp/quad-suite/master-0f52d26f` covers sphere_base, sphere_random, bolt, hand, fandisk, elk, feline, fertility, botijo, block, Hand-tri-30k, rockerarm, buddha and the crawfish scan (~/crawfish/IMG_4109.glb, 8 GB heap). Every mesh reports MATCH against the master baseline: the same status (a mesh master fails on must fail the same way), the same count signature, and an identical screenshot. The per-mesh stage times before/after go in changes-made. A DIFF stops for a user ruling.
testing-plan: 1. On master: run-scene quad-layout three times, record the stage time and counts, take a screenshot. 2. In the worktree: the same three runs plus a profile capture; compare times and counts. 3. image-diff the two screenshots. 4. mvn test for the touched packages.
unknowns: Whether the stage can reach 100 ms without changing its output; if not, what the floor is and why
changes-made: Baseline (botijo, alpha=15, cold JVM, alternated, n=3): master cross field 0.419/0.499/0.416 s (median 0.419), worktree 0.423/0.401/0.402 s (median 0.402); screenshot sha256 22e54fa9...ef70 on all six. Warm (same JVM, ixdar-cli model botijo x3): 0.188, 0.137, 0.137 s; warm split assemble 24 ms, solve aligned 59 ms (AMD + PARDISO), populate 18-28 ms, hopf 11 ms. Cold split: assemble 92, solve aligned 157, populate 48, load vector 21, hopf 21, frames/kappa ~30, metric+context ~50 ms.

Milestone 1 (crossfield/ only, output bit-identical, botijo screenshot sha 22e54fa9 unchanged): (a) SectionIntegrals.stiffnessSeries + series-taking stiffnessOffDiagonal: the 4 stiffness and 2 mass Chebyshev series are evaluated once per triangle instead of once per edge (18 -> 6 series per face), same arithmetic; (b) the AMD ordering of the realified pattern runs on another thread as soon as the pattern exists, and solveAligned factors with it via DirectSolver.factorizeWithPerm (same permutation factorize would compute); (c) the PARDISO factorization runs off-thread while the load vector and Hopf solve are built; (d) frames/transport/alignment edges and the curvature load vector are built concurrently with assembly; (e) per-face integration in assemble, the per-face theta and triangle-index loops in populate and the per-vertex singularity walk run in parallel, each writing its own slot, with all sums done sequentially in the original order; (f) principal() skips the fmod when the angle is already inside (-2pi, 2pi), where fmod returns it exactly. Unit tests CrossFieldAssembly (bit-for-bit vs reference), CrossFieldConnection, QuadLayoutNodeChain, FeatureAlignmentGuard, QuadPipelineSeam, EmbeddedTMeshPipeline, CholeskyBackendEquivalence pass.

Relaunch (agent 2): the half-done edit compiled as left; removed the moved 'active-id maps' timing log, which wt status flagged as an added diagnostic. A/B botijo under heavy machine load (load avg ~9/16 cores from sibling agents): cold master 0.405/0.480/0.391 s (median 0.405), worktree 0.309/0.541/0.397 s (median 0.397); warm master 0.195/0.128/0.136, worktree 0.202/0.153/0.130. Under contention the thread-level overlap buys almost nothing. A warm probe showed one reload at 86 ms; the critical path is the PARDISO numeric factor (31-38 ms) plus assembly and populate. Milestone 2: assemble caches each face corner's transport angle and its cos/sin, and computeTriangleIndices reuses them wherever its own rho is bit-equal (the same angle), removing 90k cos+sin pairs per solve. The 7 unit classes (18 tests) pass.

Milestone 2 timing, botijo. Cold interleaved (load avg 9-11): master 0.398/0.484/0.428 s (median 0.428), worktree 0.839 (first run after the build)/0.446/0.307 s (median 0.446); the screenshot sha is 22e54fa9 on all six. Cold numbers on this loaded machine are noise-bound. Warm, two JVMs per side x 10 reloads, alternated: master median 0.091 s (steady reloads 5-10 about 0.083 s, min 0.080); worktree median 0.064 s (steady about 0.055 s, min 0.048). Warm is under 100 ms. Cold stays about 0.3-0.45 s because the first build of each JVM runs interpreted/C1 code and loads PARDISO for the first time. On that first call, solve aligned costs 120-160 ms against 40 ms warm.

Whole suite (run_suite.py vs master-0f52d26f): 14/14 MATCH, 0 DIFF (same status, signature and screenshot). Per-mesh cross field, master -> worktree, in seconds, single cold run each under load: sphere_base 0.058->0.040, sphere_random 0.068->0.051, bolt 0.185->0.107, hand 0.176->0.138, fandisk 0.240->0.189, elk 0.363->0.220, feline 0.278->0.216, fertility 0.427->0.297, botijo 0.439->0.297, block 0.515->0.346, Hand-tri-30k 0.507->0.276, rockerarm 0.838->0.701, buddha 1.669->1.300. The four master failures fail identically. sphere_random, fandisk and Hand-tri-30k do run the cross field stage, with an identical signature, and then fail in a later stage's chart check ('winds against its patch'). crawfish fails at load on non-manifold topology and never reaches the pipeline.
